correctness.rationale: Starting from the published integral for g_{k,l}, differentiating s^{l+1}(1-s)^2 W_k verifies the difference as 2 int s^l(1-s)W_k(1-2s^k). The y=s^k transform has exact weight h_k(y)r_{k,l}(y). The derivative identity k*y*(1-y)*G_k’=-2+(1-2y)*sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(y^{j/k}-(1-y)^{j/k}) is strictly negative for 0<y<1/2, so h_k(y)>h_k(1-y). The power r is nonincreasing exactly when 0<=l<=k-2, and integral reflection makes the difference strictly positive. At y=0 the density is O(y^{(l-k+1)/k}) with exponent>-1; at y=1 it is O(1-y). The proof covers all k>=2, including boundaries; 1554 finite check assertions passed but are not infinity proofs.

A later direct treatment produced 153 exact certificates and resolved only k<=20, explicitly identifying k>=21 as open. An elementary structural reflection inequality resolves the whole infinite rod-length family, with practical relevance to finite-rod adsorption morphology and a nontrivial uniform-in-parameter gap beyond computations.
